blocks.text: VATICAN CITY — When Pope Leo XIV was elected after the pained finale of Pope Francis’ pontificate, there was hope that a younger, healthier pope would be able to guide the Catholic Church for quite some time before age and ailments slowed him. Leo’s lung cancer diagnosis announced Tuesday has thrown a question mark into that scenario and his pontificate. Already, the president of Peru is suggesting Leo’s upcoming Latin America trip may have to be changed. But Vatican watchers say the 71-year-old’s diagnosis could have other unintended effects — not all of them negative: It could propel Leo to accelerate […]...
